title: Revisiting Prophecy - A game I like more with each passing year
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrqtNoiNSdw

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to *Prophecy*, a game that has been in his life for nearly twenty years, unhappy with his earlier video and armed with fan expansions he thinks genuinely elevate it. He files it alongside *Talisman* second edition and *Runebound* second edition as the third leg of the modern adventure game — and this is one he will never sell.

The core box is competitive: ten characters circling a round globe-shaped board, having encounters, buying gear, and eventually assaulting five astral planes for the artifacts. The Dragon Realm expansion adds official co-op, which is how he plays it — two characters, with a Prophetic Dream card that periodically strengthens a Guardian, a soft timer that punishes loitering. He refuses the expansions' table-hogging auxiliary boards and instead reduces each to a single portal card seeded by the chance deck.

The real endorsement is for three fan-made decks on BGG: a quest deck that gives characters errands worth crossing the map for, and Wilderness and Civilization event decks drawn at the end of every turn. He forgets to draw them during his own demonstration turns, realises mid-video, and rewinds — which tells you how good he thinks they are.

The complaints are real: characters differ only in starting stats, the game runs long, and the circular map becomes a jumble of cards. All three, he notes, are house-ruleable.

----

Is a game you can only recommend alongside its fan expansions still a good game — or a good foundation?
